correctness.rationale: For a vanishing sum of at most p roots, split off a prime s>p from the squarefree conductor. At most p fibers are occupied, while the minimal polynomial over the remaining cyclotomic field is 1+X+…+X^(s-1); its degree s-1 follows from the coprime cyclotomic degree ratio. A missing fiber forces all coefficients to vanish, and induction on the number of primes forces exactly one occupied fiber and one p-cycle. The one-prime case follows from the same minimal polynomial over Q, and conductor 1 cannot vanish. Applying the result to exponent products a(b-b') gives a full residue set mod p and constant coordinates at r>p where the difference is nonzero. Since B has p entries, all differences nonzero mod p is equivalent to its being a transversal. The converse gives each required Fourier zero. Labeling the selected elements by their p-coordinate counts literal sets exactly once: B has r^p choices for a constant coordinate of A and r choices elsewhere; A has r choices per constant coordinate and r^p-r per nonconstant coordinate. This gives the stated multiplicities, their distinctness by unique factorization, and Q times the product of (2r^p-r). For N=30, the positive strata total 225 supported two-sets, out of 435; the weighted multiplicity total is 10125. The analytic proof, not tests, establishes all t≥1.
residual_risks: Only squarefree N with cardinality the least prime divisor is assessed; the counts do not quotient by symmetries.

evidence: A coset of the p-subgroup in CRT coordinates is all p residues in that component and constant in each other component. In products a(b-b'), the full p-coordinate requires nonzero (b-b') mod p and A bijective mod p; a constant r-coordinate means b=b' mod r or A constant mod r. Applying this to each pair gives the entire classification. Each remaining coordinate admits r choices for a constant function and r^p arbitrary functions. The union of the two one-sided constancy conditions has 2r*r^p-r² choices, independently across r.
